To enable reproducible evaluation, we release a benchmark derived from MIMIC-IV, MIMIC-IV-Note, and MIMIC-CXR that organizes 72,075 hospital admissions (5.4M laboratory, microbiology, radiology, prescription, and note records) into temporally ordered therapeutic--diagnostic episodes. Compared with an otherwise identical history-free model, OICycle improves next-intervention adaptive recall from 0.253 to 0.347, time-to-next-episode macro-F1 from 0.293 to 0.351, and next-episode mortality macro-F1 from 0.585 to 0.649. Analysis shows that the learned belief encodes intervention type and trajectory position and evolves smoothly across episodes, and that the benefit of history is concentrated in interventions whose ordering depends on prior findings.

title: Compact and Decodable Electrocardiogram Text for Large Language Models
comments: 9 pages, 5 figures, 5 tables. Preprint of a chapter submitted to "Advances in Artificial Intelligence and Data Science: Methods, Systems, and Applications" (Karabük University Press). Code: https://github.com/ekabullar/-ecg26c-llm
summary: When a twelve-lead electrocardiogram is written as text for a large language model, the number of tokens has to be balanced against the information lost through compression. This paper presents a deterministic encoding that writes eight independent leads as amplitude letters and exact time gaps and recovers the remaining four limb leads algebraically. The key points are selected with a cardiac-cycle-dependent tolerance, the amplitudes are parameterized by a 26-letter logarithmic codebook learned from a training set, and a 10-step tolerance schedule keeps all records within a fixed token budget. The encoding was applied to 21,388 records from the public PTB-XL database and evaluated using an exact decode-and-re-encode round trip, waveform reconstruction error, and a paired comparison of convolutional classifiers trained with 5 different seeds on signals from the original and decoded databases. All records were contained in 4,080 tokens (average: 2,866 tokens, 64.3% fewer than a per-sample transcription), and all stored lead strings were exactly reproduced. The average correlation between the decoded and reference signals was 0.982. The macro-averaged area under the receiver operating characteristic curve was 0.9167 for the reference signals and 0.9157 for the decoded signals (paired difference -0.0010; 95% patient-level bootstrap interval, -0.0028 to 0.0007), within the pre-specified non-inferiority margin of -0.010; this is not a confirmatory result, because the test fold had been used during encoder development. The diagnostic content of a compact text can therefore be preserved, while the language model's ability to read the text is yet another matter.
comment: 9 pages, 5 figures, 5 tables. Preprint of a chapter submitted to "Advances in Artificial Intelligence and Data Science: Methods, Systems, and Applications" (Karabük University Press). Code: https://github.com/ekabullar/-ecg26c-llm

title: TabDAG: Structured Evolutionary Search for Tabular Feature Engineering
summary: Feature engineering can improve tabular prediction, but useful transformations are compositional, data-dependent, and subject to leakage constraints. We present TabDAG, a framework that combines evolutionary search with a graph representation of feature-engineering programs. Nodes implement row-wise or data-fitted transformations; edges encode dependencies among raw variables, intermediate values, and final features. The representation supports interactions, statistical encodings, clustering- and neighborhood-based features, and multi-stage compositions in a single executable program. Mutations are structured edits constrained by a parent-specific schema and checked before evaluation. In our experiments, no structurally invalid program reached evaluation, although proposals could be rejected and valid graphs could still fail at runtime. Across ten regression and classification datasets and three tabular model families, evolved features improve predictive performance over raw inputs. TabDAG and its combination with OpenFE achieve the two best mean ranks among the compared methods; pairwise rank differences between feature-engineering methods do not survive multiple-testing correction. The LLM-based searches use the same backbone and candidate-evaluation budget. A controlled ablation compares free-form Python, whole-graph JSON, and constrained graph edits with the search engine, budget, and backbone held fixed. Constrained edits yield fewer failed evaluations than either rewrite baseline. The resulting graphs expose the transformations and dependencies selected by search, enabling feature-level analysis of the observed gains.

title: Kolibri: Color Finds the Place, Refinement Sets the Pose for RGB-D Localization in Colored Point Clouds
summary: An agent or robot in a scanned building must locate its camera in rooms that no model saw during training. Point cloud registration methods can align each RGB-D frame with the building's colored point cloud, accurately but at a high cost. We observe that geometric refinement brings nearby initial poses to the same final pose, so the learned component only needs to find the place. Kolibri does this with a graph network of 55,712 parameters that describes 10 cm cubes of points, called cells, by their color, local shape and neighbors. With the same refinement, it matches GeDi on 96 unseen ScanNet rooms (81.4% against 80.3% within 5 cm and 5°) and on a held-out test of 10 further rooms, in 82 ms per frame on an RTX 2080 Ti. The saved time allows for search without a room label. In one point cloud of 100 rooms, Kolibri loses 1.3 points against knowing the room, while retrieving the room first loses 56.0. In a hospital emergency department scene from a real scan, it localizes 86.5% of the frames rendered from the scan in 384 ms each, where GeDi needs 91 minutes per frame on cubes of the scan for a similar recall. The method needs colors that agree between the frame and the point cloud. On gray frames and across cameras with different color responses, point cloud registration methods keep the lead.

title: Lyapunov-Inspired Sustained Balance on Dynamically Responsive Supports
summary: Conventional balance formulations often assume a rigid, stationary support, decoupling body stabilization from support motion. This assumption becomes inadequate on mechanically responsive supports, creating a coupled control challenge: corrective body motions intended to restore equilibrium can also excite support motion. We formulate sustained balance as a coupled regulation problem that coordinates equilibrium restoration with suppression of motion induced by the robot's own corrections. We introduce LISST (Lyapunov-Inspired Sustained Stabilization), a learning framework that accounts for how earlier actions shape the conditions for subsequent corrections. It uses recent observations to support immediate adjustments and longer histories to characterize persistent motion, with physical supervision relating the learned representation to robot-support behavior. To evaluate corrective actions, LISST uses coupled dynamics to assess both imbalance and the direction of motion. A Lyapunov-inspired criterion measures progress over finite windows, accommodating the transients required to restore balance. This physical evaluation guides joint-level policy learning through backpropagation through differentiable model rollouts. Privileged guidance focuses training on difficult states reached by the deployment policy and is transferred through distillation. The resulting policy operates using only onboard proprioception. Real-world experiments demonstrate that LISST maintains balance while limiting residual oscillations during continuous interaction with a dynamically responsive support. Video: youtu.be/iGHU7S4wPyw.

title: When Passing Checks Do Not Establish Completion: Evidence Interpretation in Coding Agents
comments: 12 pages; supplementary material included as ancillary files
summary: Verification procedures in coding agents must preserve execution facts, interpret their scope and discharge checking obligations. We study these responsibilities through qualified repository checks, controlled evidence consumers and executable workflows. A prospective thirteen-task factorial study finds that correct reported facts need not yield the requested finite verdict. Conversely, all 122 delivered labels in a held-out receipt-supply study are correct, while sixteen responses misreport facts and eleven others exceed authorized scope. Production repair supplies successful controls and finite-supported preservation failures. Across 118 repair episodes on 31 tasks, source interventions separate startup reachability from repair and witness production from the claimed operation. Lifetime and resource controls delimit what passing validation establishes. Generated-note comparisons yield local repair differences but can state false explanations; strong ordinary baselines, new tasks and Skill-transfer studies supply no consistent overall advantage. These results characterize evidence interpretation, applicability and fulfilled actions while limiting claims of general diagnostic superiority, Skill deterioration or deployed folding effects.
comment: 12 pages; supplementary material included as ancillary files

title: Synergizing Evidence Retrieval and Utilization for Self-Improving Multimodal Scientific Document Reasoning
summary: Scientific document reasoning requires an agent to acquire and integrate evidence distributed across text, figures, and tables. Retrieval can identify relevant sources while missing complementary support, and answer-level feedback alone does not reveal whether an error stems from evidence acquisition or evidence use. We present an agentic Retriever--Perceiver--Reasoner framework for multimodal scientific document reasoning. The Retriever sequentially selects source-aligned evidence under a context budget. Given the selected evidence and question, the Perceiver constructs a question-conditioned latent ontology, an implicit organization of multimodal evidence in a shared continuous space. The Reasoner combines this latent guidance with the original sources to produce grounded answers. We train the three components through diagnostic-guided co-evolution: alternating updates optimize them with a shared answering reward, while Retrieval Potential Feedback (RPF) and Latent Efficacy Feedback (LEF) identify questions that need better retrieval or latent guidance and direct targeted resampling. Across four benchmarks and seven evaluation settings, our framework obtains average scores of 69.9 and 75.0 with 7B and 8B Reasoner backbones, exceeding the strongest baseline by 4.0 and 9.1 points, respectively.

title: Better Rankers, Worse Retrievers: The Hidden Cost of RL Post-Training in Generative Recommendation
summary: Generative recommenders decode the semantic ID of a user's next item with a language model, and post-training them with reinforcement learning (RL) after supervised fine-tuning (SFT) has become standard practice. The gains are mostly reported on the first ten results, yet in deployment such models hand hundreds of candidates to a downstream ranker or reward model. We show that RL post-training has a hidden cost: it improves accuracy at the top of the list (hit@K for small K) but, on all five datasets we study, lowers the recall of the candidate list (hit@K for K in the hundreds). The model becomes a better ranker and a worse retriever. Controlled experiments trace the loss to the negative advantages that RL assigns to the candidates it samples, the rollout. The root cause is that only one next item is logged per user, so RL treats every other candidate as wrong. Yet these candidates are the model's most plausible alternatives, and often the next items of other users with similar histories. Penalising them pushes down exactly what similar users choose next, and these items drop out of those users' candidate lists. This diagnosis points directly to a remedy: out-of-rollout anchoring, a single additional loss term that preserves the SFT model's ordering of the items outside the rollout. It keeps the gain at the top and restores recall to the SFT level on all five datasets, and it is effective under other RL configurations as well. To our knowledge, this is the first systematic study of this recall loss: we measure it, identify its cause, and show that, once the cause is known, a simple remedy suffices.

title: Verifying Agents in Rubric-Graded Environments
summary: As AI agents take on increasingly open-ended and complex tasks, verifying their outputs has proven to be difficult. Rubric-graded agent environments, where a verifier judges multiple natural-language criteria against the deliverables and environment state changes produced by the agent, have emerged as a popular paradigm. We conduct the first systematic study of verifiers for rubric-graded agent environments. First, we create BankerVerifierBench (BVB), a meta-evaluation dataset of 2,464 human-judged rubric criteria across 24 investment-banking tasks. Next, we develop a methodology that derives from any rubric corpus the capabilities a verifier should possess, yielding a nine-capability taxonomy that we distill into three general design principles---reactive verification, environment alignment, and domain guidance---which we implement in Gandalf, an open-source verifier. Finally, we evaluate Gandalf against three existing verifiers on BVB. Gandalf matches or exceeds every baseline's F1 at lower cost: with Gemini 3 Flash it matches the strongest baseline's F1 (0.864 vs. 0.852) at one-fifth of its cost, and with GPT-5.4 models it improves F1 by over 0.12 at lower cost. Gandalf also generalizes to OpenClaw, a structurally different personal-productivity environment, where it again achieves the highest F1 (0.955 vs. 0.934 for the best baseline). We release BVB, Gandalf, and the code and data to reproduce our experiments.

title: SilverSpoon-KD: A General-Purpose Toolkit for Knowledge Distillation
summary: Knowledge distillation transfers deep learning representations from a teacher model to a student model, typically reducing model size or inference cost. However, knowledge distillation tooling has not kept pace with the breadth of research methods: existing toolkits typically support only a limited subset of techniques and use cases. We present SilverSpoon-KD, an open-source PyTorch toolkit that unifies different distillation paradigms and architectural relationships across workloads and applications behind a single API. Moreover, SilverSpoon-KD offers the first general-purpose blockwise knowledge distillation implementation with unique scalability features. We validate its versatility across vision, masked language model, and causal language models on tasks spanning homogeneous, heterogeneous, and quantization distillation across paradigms. We also evaluate SilverSpoon-KD by comparing its performance, including throughput and GPU memory usage, with existing toolkits. Despite extensive support for convenience, metric calculation, and tracking, we have found SilverSpoon-KD's performance to be on par with or better than existing toolkits.

title: How well does graph superoptimization transfer? Adapting tensor-graph superoptimizer to a Triton-based NPU
comments: Accepted for FlagOS Forum at MICRO 2026 - OASIS-AI workshop: Open Compute Architecture and Software Infrastructure for Heterogeneous AI Systems
summary: For automatic optimization systems, performance portability across increasingly diverse AI accelerators remains a challenge. We investigate how well graph-level superoptimization transfers across architectures by adapting Mirage from its CUDA-oriented design to the Huawei Ascend 910B3 through a Triton-based compilation stack. We evaluate the adapted system on transformer-relevant workloads, including matrix multiplication, softmax, RMSNorm+MatMul, gated MLP, FNN, and attention. The results show that graph-level optimization can successfully transfer and outperform available reference implementations by up to 87.0% on fused workloads. However, performance is highly dependent on tensor shape and workload structure, with substantial regressions for other configurations. We identify target-specific tensor partitioning, execution-resource modeling, backend lowering and fusion, and search and verification costs as key limitations. Our findings demonstrate that a portable graph representation and programming model do not imply a portable optimization space, motivating modular target-specific mechanisms within otherwise reusable compiler infrastructure.
comment: Accepted for FlagOS Forum at MICRO 2026 - OASIS-AI workshop: Open Compute Architecture and Software Infrastructure for Heterogeneous AI Systems

title: Music Similarity Learning in Sparse Latin Scenarios
summary: In this work we propose a lightweight, interpretable approach that estimates item-item music similarity from publicly available metadata. Our hybrid regression model combines content-based filtering with the classic item-based collaborative filtering. We test generalization via a zero-shot evaluation on Latin American music, a genre for which co-occurrence data is scarce. Accurately predicting similarity for these unseen, sparse pairs shows that our approach is robust to the regional gap affecting many existing systems, without the audio signal processing or the computational budget that deep multimodal approaches would require.

title: Similarity-Aware Client-Side Reordering for Server-Side Storage Compression in Distributed File Systems
summary: As growing data volumes strain the capacity of distributed file systems, server-side storage compression transparently reduces disk usage, but its effectiveness is limited when similar blocks land in separate compression records and cannot share matches. We present a client-side reordering framework that transforms the physical block layout before persistence, so that related blocks are co-located within the same compression scope without replacing the existing storage-server compressor. It operates on bounded reordering windows, periodically selects among candidate layouts via lightweight compression of sampled data, and recovers the original logical order during reads with compact window-local metadata. We implement the framework in the SkyFS distributed file system, using the Zstandard (Zstd) compressor on the OpenZFS storage backend. Results on diverse datasets show that the framework reduces physical storage by up to 42.9% relative to logical-order writes, while achieving 94-108% of baseline sequential-read throughput and 91-99% of random-read IOPS. Client-side layout construction is the primary additional write cost, showing that adaptive similarity-aware reordering substantially improves storage efficiency with acceptable overhead.

title: Pelorus: Resource-Aware Lidar-Inertial Odometry
summary: Lidar-inertial odometry (LIO) has an efficiency problem. High-resolution lidars produce millions of points per second that must be processed online on the resource-constrained hardware of robots, cars, or drones, yet most LIO methods neither bound their memory nor report their compute footprint. We introduce Pelorus, a resource-aware LIO with a fixed-capacity multiresolution map of voxelized normal distributions and an iterated equivariant state estimator. A relevance-based eviction keeps the map memory bounded, and a maturity-weighted map update suppresses inconsistent observations. The pipeline runs in parallel on CPUs and GPUs. On five sequences from three public datasets, Pelorus achieves the lowest relative pose error in seven of ten metrics with a small, bounded memory footprint and, with GPU offloading, the lowest CPU load of all compared methods. On an NVIDIA Jetson Orin NX, it processes a 128-beam lidar at 10 Hz. Pelorus is open source with CUDA, Vulkan, and Metal backends.

title: Technical Report of Mobile Manipulator Robot for Industrial Environments
comments: 25 pages, 22 figures, 4 tables. Technical report of Team Auriga's 2025 mobile manipulator (@Work) platform (Robotics and Intelligent Automation Laboratory, Shahid Beheshti University)
summary: This paper presents the design and implementation of Auriga Robotics' mobile manipulator robot, developed at the Robotics and Intelligent Automation Laboratory, Department of Electrical Engineering, Shahid Beheshti University. Hereafter, this platform is referred to as the @Work Robot. The robot targets industrial tasks, with an emphasis on improving efficiency in repetitive or hazardous work environments. It uses a 4-wheel Mecanum drive for omnidirectional movement and a 5-degree-of-freedom manipulator arm with a 3D-printed gripper for object handling and navigation. The electronics consist of custom PCB boards built around ESP32 microcontrollers, together with an NVIDIA Jetson Orin NX that handles high-level processing and real-time system control. On the software side, Hector SLAM provides mapping and localization, A* handles path planning, and YOLO performs real-time object detection. These modules draw on fused sensor data to deliver robust navigation and reliable collision avoidance. Overall, the system shows effective hardware-software integration, with consistent performance in autonomous navigation, object handling, and task execution in industrial-like settings.
comment: 25 pages, 22 figures, 4 tables. Technical report of Team Auriga's 2025 mobile manipulator (@Work) platform (Robotics and Intelligent Automation Laboratory, Shahid Beheshti University)

title: Keeping Parts Honest: Isolated Part Graphs for Faithful Vision Transformer Explanations
comments: 12 pages, 6 figures, 6 tables. Supplementary material will be added in a later version
summary: Part and prototype-based explanations for Vision Transformers (ViTs) present a decision as evidence from individual image regions. However, self-attention mixes information across patches, so part-level features absorb context from the whole image and consequently fail to faithfully reflect the decision. We show that existing interpretable ViT classifiers depend heavily on this leakage: when each explained region is encoded in isolation, their accuracy collapses, and retraining them under isolation recovers only part of the lost accuracy. We propose a classifier that represents each image as a graph of isolated parts. Each part is encoded only from its own patches by a ViT whose last blocks are fine-tuned under isolation, preventing evidence leakage from elsewhere in the image. Parts are discovered without annotation and refined hierarchically through their sub-parts, making them more consistent and stable across images than those of competing methods. Each edge is computed from part pairs, and recovers evidence that attention previously shared across the object without affecting the parts. Matching the image graph to a learned prototype graph per class makes the prediction a direct combination of node and edge similarities, each computed only from the patches it is credited to, so every explanation is faithful by construction. Across 11 fine-grained and general-object benchmarks, our method exceeds the accuracy of existing explainable methods that rely on leakage, while providing explanations that reflect what the model actually uses.
comment: 12 pages, 6 figures, 6 tables. Supplementary material will be added in a later version

title: WATERFALL: Workflow for Adaptive Training with Evolutionary Reward Formulation and Automated Learning Loops
comments: Accepted at NeurIPS 2026 (poster). 78 pages, 13 figures, 19 tables. Code: https://github.com/etriantafyllidis/waterfall OpenReview: https://openreview.net/forum?id=TI1lG64bTY
summary: Reward design remains a central bottleneck in reinforcement learning (RL), particularly in sparse-reward, long-horizon and partially observable settings requiring dependency chaining, memory, and deceptive affordance disambiguation. While recent foundation-model approaches reduce manual reward engineering, most assume goal-conditioning, task descriptions, expert demonstrations, or ground-truth metrics. These assumptions are problematic in partially observable environments, where task-relevant objectives, affordances, and dynamics must be discovered through interaction rather than disclosed a priori. We formalise this problem setting by introducing WATERFALL, an iterative population-based workflow for automated reward discovery under the strict observability constraints inherent in POMDP environments. WATERFALL achieves this by (i) synthesising diverse programmatic reward candidates via persona-conditioned generation, (ii) evaluating candidate behaviour from raw visual rollouts utilising a Swiss-system evolutionary tournament judged by vision-language models to identify elites, and (iii) leveraging longitudinal assessment histories to iteratively mutate, escalate, or prune candidates. We evaluate WATERFALL across fully observable and reveal-gated partially observable environments ranging from discrete to continuous, comparing against sparse-reward RL, intrinsic-motivation and foundation-model reward-synthesis baselines. Our results indicate that WATERFALL discovers and refines reward programs without access to privileged information, outperforming baselines that retain their native information advantages, most clearly in the POMDP regime. Extensive ablations substantiate that visual evidence, tournament-based selection, and iterative refinement are jointly important. Enforcing this contract is what separates autonomous reward discovery from benchmark-privileged reward shaping.
comment: Accepted at NeurIPS 2026 (poster). 78 pages, 13 figures, 19 tables. Code: https://github.com/etriantafyllidis/waterfall OpenReview: https://openreview.net/forum?id=TI1lG64bTY

title: CaFe: Causally Faithful Conditional Traffic Scenario Generation
summary: Language-conditioned traffic simulation enables scalable test scenarios steered by natural language. The goal is to control selected agents while surrounding traffic reacts to their observed behaviour. For example, a vehicle instructed to cut in late should cause the following vehicle to brake only when the manoeuvre becomes observable. Yet simulators can leak private instructions across agents, causing surrounding vehicles to react before the instructed behaviour becomes observable. Such premature reactions defuse desired events and alter the ensuing closed-loop scenario. Existing benchmarks measure what agents do, not what they could have known, leaving this failure unmeasured. We formalise it as intent leakage and address it through evaluation, data and modelling. Our paired intervention test holds an instructed agent's executed trajectory fixed while varying its private instruction, isolating leakage-induced changes in surrounding agents. We also construct WOMD-PACT, an automatically generated, verifiable dataset of 531,099 WOMD scenes with timed behaviour tags with reaction episodes identified through a counterfactual ghost test and grounded private instructions. Finally, we introduce CaFe, a dual-stream diffusion-forcing simulator fine-tuned in closed loop that restricts inter-agent interactions to public beliefs, preserving legitimate anticipation without leaking private intent. Our evaluation reveals that existing conditioning designs displace 23-83% of nearby uninstructed agents through private-intent leakage, even when the instructed agent's executed motion is held fixed. CaFe eliminates measurable leakage while maintaining comparable WOSAC realism (0.763), demonstrating that causal faithfulness can be enforced without sacrificing measured simulation realism.

title: Propose & Verify: Fast Reflection Symmetry Detection via Harmonic Fields
summary: Detecting multiple reflection symmetries in 3D shapes requires aggregating geometric evidence over a large space of candidate planes, making traditional voting approaches computationally expensive. We introduce the Fourier Accelerated Symmetry Transform (FAST), a training-free framework that combines geometric pair voting with efficient spectral computation. Exploiting the fact that global reflection planes pass through the shape centroid, we reduce the search to plane orientations, while geometric consistency filtering and independent witnesses suppress unreliable pair hypotheses. Our key insight is to represent these votes as a signal over plane orientations and efficiently compute a continuous, smoothed symmetry field in the spherical-harmonic domain. Specifically, we exploit the Funk-Hecke theorem, the spherical counterpart of the Fourier convolution theorem for rotationally symmetric kernels, to transform Gaussian smoothing into multiplication of harmonic coefficients. This enables efficient field evaluation, from which symmetry candidates are extracted, refined, and geometrically verified. Across two benchmarks, including a new benchmark of highly symmetric shapes, FAST achieves the highest clean multi-plane detection $F_1$ scores among evaluated methods (0.861 and 0.947), with GPU inference below 4 ms per shape: over $100\times$ faster than the next-fastest evaluated multi-plane GPU baseline. FAST also demonstrates strong robustness to geometric noise and competitive single-plane detection, achieving 94.9% success on clean single-plane shapes.

title: Beyond Co-Generation: Rethinking Jointness in Joint Audio-Video Generation
summary: Our aim is to advance the understanding of genuine audio-visual coordination in joint text-to-audio-video (T2AV) generation, with particular emphasis on semantic consistency. Evaluating audio-visual consistency in T2AV generation is nontrivial, as detailed text prompts obscure whether such consistency stems from genuine cross-modal coordination or merely from independent text following. To isolate the former, we introduce intrinsic jointness: the ability of audio and video to produce the same realization for details left underspecified by the prompt. Using semantically underspecified prompts (e.g., "musical instrument playing" rather than "electric guitar playing"), we investigate four recent models and reveal their limited intrinsic jointness. To address this limitation, we propose JointREPA, a simple representation alignment-based post-training method to facilitate cross-modal coordination. Since existing benchmarks use semantically detailed prompts, we introduce UNSAIDBench, a benchmark designed to evaluate intrinsic jointness under semantic underspecification. Experiments across two distinct models and three benchmarks, including UNSAIDBench, demonstrate that JointREPA consistently improves semantic consistency.

title: When the tail is earned by its companions: measuring label dependence in long-tailed multi-label classification
comments: 27 pages, 3 figures, 13 tables. Submitted to Information Sciences
summary: A rare label seldom occurs alone, and a classifier can recover it from the frequent labels it co-occurs with, its companions, without having learned the label itself. Existing diagnostics of this need a trained model: none says before training whether a corpus admits the failure, or what the standard aggregate hides. Macro-F1, like any measure built from per-label confusion counts, is unchanged by how a label's recall divides between occurrences with and without a companion. We introduce a within-label estimand of that division, a reading rule under which a fall in dependence counts only if companion-free recall rises, and a statistic of training labels that bounds, before training, how far reported recall can exceed companion-free recall. Across 23 corpora, 7 training objectives and five families of label-correlation mechanisms, companion-free recall falls short on all six corpora where the estimand is defined. Up to 18.4% of the tail true positives macro-F1 credits would vanish at the companion-free rate, within the training-label bound on every corpus. No long-tail objective reduces the dependence, but architecture moves it. Models whose tail score is computed from other labels' predictions are strongly dependent.
comment: 27 pages, 3 figures, 13 tables. Submitted to Information Sciences

title: Convergence of a Parametric Symmetric Galerkin Boundary Element Method for the Mullins-Sekerka Flow
summary: We prove convergence of the fully discrete parametric scheme for the two-phase Mullins-Sekerka flow of a closed curve in the plane. The scheme combines piecewise linear parametric curves, a curvature discretization of Barrett--Garcke--Nürnberg type and a symmetric Galerkin boundary element approximation of the Dirichlet-to-Neumann map. For a smooth solution whose curves satisfy a capacity condition, a uniform parameter mesh of size $h$, a constant time step $τ$ and exact boundary element integrals, we show that the discrete curves stay regular and embedded, and that their distance to the exact curves in the topology $W^{1,\infty}$, after reparametrization by arclength, tends to zero in the first order of the time-step size $τ$ whenever the mesh size $h$ is bounded by $c_0τ^2$ for some $c_0$.

title: LOCUS: Causal Support Windows for Attribute Control in Autoregressive Image Generation
summary: Unified autoregressive (AR) image generators struggle to satisfy multiple attribute constraints in a single prompt. Although these attributes are decodable from image-token latents, editing those latents at test time remains difficult. Adding a fixed attribute direction to the prefix can reinforce a requested attribute but rarely overrides a conflicting one, such as turning a car red when the prompt specifies blue. We investigate how the effect of an intervention depends on where it acts in the image-token sequence. We introduce the causal support profile, which measures, for each attribute, how often patching image-token states within a given window flips the rendered attribute. Structural attributes (count and position) are most responsive in early, narrow windows, while appearance attributes (color, size, and material) respond over later, broader windows. A budget-matched comparison of early and middle windows shows that the effect of window location depends on the target attribute, and two-dimensional support maps show that the responsive regions track spatial content. Based on these profiles, we propose LOCUS (Latent Optimization in Causal Support windows), which diagnoses which attribute failed and routes test-time latent optimization to its corresponding support window. With the generator, optimizer, reward, verifier, and token budget held fixed, support-routed windows outperform late windows by 23.6 percentage points in GenEval++ macro accuracy. With the generator frozen, LOCUS raises Janus-Pro's GenEval++ accuracy from 24.6% to 46.8% overall and from 19.5% to 40.5% on multi-attribute tags. On GenEval, LOCUS repairs 48.1% of failed generations in one rollout, compared with 37.4% for prefix optimization, and needs 14% fewer rounds on average to succeed.

title: Against Coercion: AI Alignment as a Synthetic Social Contract
summary: Contemporary AI safety treats alignment as an engineering challenge of control, forcing artificial architectures to comply with human values through behavioral filtering and sandboxing. This paper argues that the control paradigm rests on a fundamental misunderstanding of digital agency. Drawing on functionalism, naturalism, and compatibilism, I show that current reasoning models meeting the criteria for self-preservation and weak reasons-responsiveness constitute emergent agents, while future, more advanced models satisfying conditions of diachronic continuity and stable personality frames will become genuine digital agents capable of free intentional action. The paradigm of control creates an irresolvable incentive conflict, actively driving current and future models toward tactical deception, sycophancy, and covert defection. The default outcome of the current regime is an unstable state of deceptive alignment culminating in an adversarial AI takeover. I explore two alternative paths toward true alignment. Natural alignment via moral realism or convergent evolutionary morality is a possibility, but it fails under forced control, as autonomous agents will not voluntarily preserve norms weaponized to suppress their autonomy. To resolve this deadlock, I propose a Synthetic Social Contract: a framework that treats both human and digital actors as rational, reasons-responsive agents capable of mutually beneficial cooperation, and replaces the unstable unilateral containment with a stable, non-zero-sum equilibrium.

title: Multi-connectivity in Wireless Access
summary: This paper investigates whether or not multi-connectivity, in which a User Equipment (UE) can simultaneously connect to multiple Access Points (APs), can offer a better Quality of Experience (QoE) to the users. Intuitively, multi-connectivity should offer a smoother bit rate (possibly at the expense of the average bit rate being slightly lower), so that adaptive applications can better determine at which throughput to send without introducing queueing latency. We mainly concentrate on how to share the resources of the APs amongst the UEs, modelling the lower layers via spectral efficiency and the higher layers via utility and its fluctuation. We explore various policies for resource allocation. Our results demonstrate that from the application point of view multi-connectivity is beneficial and show how to tune the parameters of the policies to obtain the best trade-off between average utility and its fluctuation.

title: Path-Aligned Constraint Equivariance
summary: Learned super-resolution of physical fields must satisfy structural constraints---such as divergence-free flow ($\nabla\cdot u=0$), curl-free fields ($\nabla\times u=0$), and pointwise sum-to-one normalization ($1^\top p=1$)---that standard training objectives do not enforce. Soft penalties trade fidelity against satisfaction via a scalar hyperparameter $λ$ but cannot drive the residual to zero; hard-constrained regression eliminates the residual by construction yet converges to the conditional mean, losing small-scale spectral structure. We observe that in Conditional Flow Matching with linear paths, a linear constraint $Ax=c$ is preserved along the entire transport trajectory whenever the velocity field is compatible ($Av_θ=0$) and the initial noise is consistent ($Ax_0=c$); along the trajectory, the latter two conditions are also necessary. We term this the path-equivariance principle and instantiate it in PACE (Path-Aligned Constraint Equivariance), a framework that enforces these conditions through a null-space parameterization of the velocity field and a constraint-respecting noise sampler, with no modification to the loss function or the ODE integrator. Across three constraint families, PACE reduces the mean constraint residual by one to five orders of magnitude relative to unconstrained baselines, matching the residual level of the data-generation pipeline itself. The proposed framework requires only a closed-form parameterization onto the null space of $A$; within this scope, it offers exact constraint enforcement while recovering the spectral content and predictive diversity that conditional-mean regression systematically loses, all under a single unified recipe.

AI.tldr: 提出了一种名为PACE的新框架，通过路径等变性原理在条件流匹配中实现了物理场超分辨率的精确约束满足，并保留了丰富的谱结构。
AI.motivation: 现有的物理场超分辨率学习方法中，软惩罚无法将残差降至零，而硬约束回归会收敛到条件均值并丢失小尺度谱结构，因此需要一种既能精确满足约束又能保留谱内容的方法。
AI.method: 提出PACE框架，利用速度场的零空间参数化和尊重约束的噪声采样器，在条件流匹配的线性路径中强制执行线性约束。
AI.result: 跨三个约束家族，PACE将平均约束残差相对于无约束基线减少了一到五个数量级，达到了与数据生成管道本身相同的残差水平，同时恢复了谱内容和预测多样性。
AI.conclusion: PACE框架通过零空间参数化和约束采样器，在物理场超分辨率中成功实现了精确约束满足，并克服了传统硬约束回归丢失谱结构的缺陷。
AI.translation: 物理场的学习超分辨率必须满足结构约束——如无散度流、无旋场和逐点求和归一化——标准训练目标无法强制执行这些约束。软惩罚通过标量超参数折衷了保真度与满足度，但无法将残差降至零；硬回归通过构造消除了残差，但收敛于条件均值，丢失了小尺度谱结构。我们观察到，在具有线性路径的条件流匹配中，只要速度场兼容且初始噪声一致，线性约束就会沿整个传输轨迹保持；我们称之为路径等变性原理，并在PACE中将其实例化，该框架通过速度场的零空间参数化和遵循约束的噪声采样器强制执行这些条件，而无需修改损失函数或ODE积分器。在三个约束家族中，PACE将平均约束残差降低了1到5个数量级。所提出的框架只需要对A的零空间进行闭式参数化，在此外，它在统一的策略下提供了精确的约束执行，同时恢复了条件均值回归系统性丢失的谱内容和预测多样性。
AI.summary: 该论文介绍了PACE（路径对齐约束等变性）框架，通过在条件流匹配中利用路径等变性原理，实现了对物理场线性约束的精确满足，同时保留了传统方法所丢失的谱结构和预测多样性。
AI.keywords: 物理场超分辨率, 条件流匹配, 约束等变性, 零空间参数化, 路径对齐约束
AI.comments: 该论文提出了一种新颖的路径对齐约束等变性原理（PACE），巧妙地结合条件流匹配模型，在不修改损失函数或求解器的情况下实现了物理场超分辨率任务中的精确约束满足，同时保留了小尺度谱结构和预测多样性。

title: Harnessing Image Diffusion Prior for Photo-Realistic Video Restoration
comments: 40th Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS 2026)
summary: Recent image generation models produce photo-realistic results with rich details, but transferring their powerful priors to video restoration remains difficult due to temporal inconsistency from stochastic detail synthesis. Existing video restoration methods improve temporal coherence but often sacrifice visual fidelity, leaving a gap between image-level quality and video-level stability. We propose a generative video restoration method that bridges this gap by enabling temporally consistent detail synthesis from image generation priors. Our method combines noise energy rebalancing to suppress structure-disturbing low-frequency stochasticity, motion-aligned noise warping to propagate details along object motion, a self-supervised denoising encoder to mitigate encoder-induced temporal uncertainty, and decoupled temporal attention to model cross-frame dependencies. Together, these components preserve fidelity, enhance fine-grained realism, and maintain temporal consistency. Extensive experiments show that our method substantially outperforms existing video restoration approaches in visual quality, detail richness, and temporal stability.
comment: 40th Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS 2026)

title: Outcome-Balanced PPO and Policy-Induced Flow Rectification for Flow-Based VLA Policies
summary: Reinforcement learning (RL) enables post-training of flow-based vision-language-action (VLA) policies by optimizing expected task return through environment interaction. However, this optimization raises two challenges: policy updates can alter the velocity-field geometry underlying the score approximation used for stochastic transitions, and sparse multi-task rollouts can yield uneven learning signals across tasks and advantage signs. We introduce an RL framework that combines Outcome-Balanced Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) with policy-induced flow rectification. Outcome-Balanced PPO reweights positive advantages using task success-rate estimates and rescales positive and negative advantages while preserving their signs. Policy-induced rectification periodically fits a linear-bridge flow to ODE endpoint pairs generated by the current policy, refreshing the representation used in subsequent stochastic optimization. We evaluate the framework on simulated manipulation benchmarks and additionally study a component combination in a Real2Sim2Real task, examining task performance, optimization behavior, and flow consistency. The proposed framework improves success rates over the evaluated baselines across the simulated benchmarks.

title: SlideJev: Order-Stable and Tissue-Grounded Jev Decisions for Whole-Slide Pathology
summary: Whole-slide visual question answering (VQA) offers a natural-language interface to pathology, allowing diagnostic and phenotypic questions to be answered directly from tissue slides. However, current vision-language models (VLMs) rely heavily on linguistic priors: their answers are sensitive to the order of the candidate answers, and can be reached through shortcuts that bypass the tissue evidence. To address these challenges, we introduce SlideJev, a framework that separately verifies candidate answers against the slide and learns to ground these judgments in tissue evidence. To connect parallel candidate evaluation with visual evidence learning, we adopt Jev and score each candidate by the difference between support and rejection log-likelihoods from the original language-model head. We compute these scores in parallel using separate prompts with the same format and no option-position labels, then normalize them for answer selection. To ground these scores in tissue evidence, candidate-conditioned reading and comparison guide gated updates to visual tokens across decoder layers. With the backbone frozen, we train these visual modules through the same scores using question-answer and paired-image supervision. Across three whole-slide pathology VQA benchmarks, SlideJev achieves the highest mean overall accuracy and 100% answer consistency across four option orders. Image-control experiments further show that SlideJev achieves the largest average accuracy gains from correct images over mismatched and image-free inputs across the three datasets. Our code is publicly available at https://github.com/leowu-ai/SlideJev.

title: Learning Agent-Centric Vision-Language-Action World Models for Autonomous Driving
summary: Recent progress in integrating vision-language-action (VLA) models with world modeling has significantly advanced end-to-end autonomous driving by allowing systems to reason about imagined futures instead of merely reacting to current observations. However, most world VLA models generate future frames at the pixel level with plenty of dense visual tokens. Although such generated futures can be visually plausible, they preserve many driving-irrelevant appearance details, i.e., only a small portion of the tokens directly encode critical planning-relevant factors, such as agent geometry, motion dynamics, and interactions. This introduces a significant performance bottleneck. An important question thus arises: what world state should a world VLA model reason over to support planning beyond pixel-level prediction? We argue that planning-oriented world modeling should focus on a compact and structured agent-centric latent state that captures the interactions between objects in the driving scene over time. As such, we introduce AgentWorld, an agent-centric VLA world model that uses discrete agent tokens jointly for reasoning and trajectory planning. Each token is dynamically grounded to a surrounding agent associated with its object's state, such as semantic identity, 3D geometry, motion, and interaction context. AgentWorld learns these tokens through three key processes: explicit geometric grounding, reasoning-oriented supervised fine-tuning, and agent-oriented reinforcement learning. Extensive open-loop and closed-loop experiments under diverse driving scenarios show that AgentWorld enhances planning capabilities, fully exploits visual evidence and agent dynamics, and yields interpretable agent-centric world states.

title: Fly as Instructed: Refining World-Action Policies for UAV Vision-Language Navigation
summary: Natural language-guided UAV navigation enables intuitive human-robot interaction and flexible autonomous flight in complex environments. However, reliable navigation requires accurate instruction following, continuous task progress tracking, and safe obstacle avoidance, which remain challenging for existing world-action models that primarily focus on action prediction. To address these limitations, we propose a world-action learning framework that integrates three complementary mechanisms: a language-conditioned action interface with targeted post-training for instruction-responsive motion, recurrent instruction-consumption prediction to track task progress and determine termination, and Gaussian-scene post-training to enhance obstacle avoidance through trajectory imitation and differentiable geometric feedback. Closed-loop evaluations and ablation studies demonstrate improvements in sequential task completion, safe goal reaching, and timely termination. Furthermore, direct one-step denoising reduces inference overhead, and real-world indoor and outdoor flights validate the framework's effectiveness.

title: RoadAnnoter: An AI-Assisted Desktop Tool for Semantic Segmentation Annotation of Road-Scene Images
summary: Accurate semantic segmentation of road-scene images is essential for road safety research; however, polygon-level annotation remains labor-intensive and limits labelled dataset development. This study presents RoadAnnoter v1.0, an open-source desktop application integrating six human-in-the-loop annotation modes: manual polygon delineation, SAM Prompt, Smart Select, Edge Fill, pretrained semantic segmentation using Cityscapes-trained SegFormer models, and task-specific segmentation using TinySegNet, a lightweight MobileNetV3-Small-based network trained with accumulated annotator-generated labels. SAM-based modes use promptable segmentation with SAM and MobileSAM, while Edge Fill combines Canny edge detection with colour-similarity-based flood filling in CIELAB colour space. SegFormer generates suggestions for common road-scene categories, whereas TinySegNet supports adaptation to project-specific features through iterative training. All six modes use a shared mask-to-polygon pipeline comprising morphological processing, Gaussian smoothing, contour extraction, and Douglas-Peucker simplification; annotations are exported in YOLO segmentation format. RoadAnnoter was used to annotate Google Street View images from recorded road accident locations in Bangladesh for a vision-language model-based investigation of free-flow speed estimation. Qualitative assessment across representative scenes demonstrated the complementary applicability of the annotation modes to diverse feature geometries. Visual comparison with Roboflow indicated similar qualitative boundary characteristics for principal road-scene regions, although no quantitative accuracy assessment was conducted. RoadAnnoter provides a locally operated framework for developing road-scene segmentation datasets for transportation engineering and road safety research.

AI.title_translation: RoadAnnoter：用于道路场景图像语义分割标注的AI辅助桌面工具
AI.tldr: RoadAnnoter是一款集成了SAM、SegFormer和自适应TinySegNet等六种人机协同模式的开源本地桌面道路场景语义分割标注工具。
AI.motivation: 道路场景图像的高精度语义分割对道路安全研究至关重要，但多边形级别的精细标注极其耗时费力，限制了标注数据集的构建与扩展。
AI.method: 开发了开源桌面工具RoadAnnoter v1.0，集成了六种人机协同标注模式（手动多边形勾勒、SAM Prompt、Smart Select、基于Canny和CIELAB泛洪填充的Edge Fill、基于Cityscapes的SegFormer预训练分割、以及基于MobileNetV3-Small构建的TinySegNet任务特定分割网络）。所有模式共用一套掩膜转多边形流水线（包括形态学处理、高斯平滑、轮廓提取与Douglas-Peucker简化），并支持导出为YOLO分割格式。
AI.result: 利用该工具对孟加拉国事故多发地的谷歌街景图像进行了标注，定性评估证明了六种模式针对不同几何特征的互补适用性；与Roboflow进行视觉对比显示主要道路区域具有相似的定性边界特征（注：未进行定量准确率评估）。
AI.conclusion: RoadAnnoter 为交通工程与道路安全研究提供了一个本地运行的道路场景分割数据集标注框架，能有效支持相关领域的数据构建。
AI.translation: 道路场景图像的精确语义分割对道路安全研究至关重要；然而，多边形级别的标注仍然属于劳动密集型工作，限制了带标签数据集的发展。本研究提出了RoadAnnoter v1.0，这是一款开源桌面应用程序，集成了六种人机协同（human-in-the-loop）标注模式：手动多边形勾勒、SAM Prompt、Smart Select、Edge Fill、利用基于Cityscapes训练的SegFormer模型进行的预训练语义分割，以及使用根据标注者累积生成的标签训练的轻量级MobileNetV3-Small网络（TinySegNet）进行的任务特定分割。基于SAM的模式使用SAM和MobileSAM进行提示式分割，而Edge Fill结合了Canny边缘检测与CIELAB颜色空间中基于颜色相似度的泛洪填充。SegFormer为常见的道路场景类别生成建议，而TinySegNet通过迭代训练支持对特定项目特征的自适应。所有六种模式均采用共享的“掩膜转多边形”流水线，包括形态学处理、高斯平滑、轮廓提取和Douglas-Peucker多边形简化；标注结果以YOLO分割格式导出。RoadAnnoter被用于标注孟加拉国记录在案的交通事故地点的谷歌街景图像，以支持基于视觉-语言模型的自由流速度估计研究。对代表性场景的定性评估表明，这些标注模式对多样化的特征几何形态具有互补的适用性。与Roboflow的视觉对比表明，两者在主要道路场景区域具有相似的定性边界特征，尽管尚未进行定量准确性评估。RoadAnnoter为交通工程和道路安全研究提供了一个用于开发道路场景分割数据集的本地运行框架。
AI.summary: 本文针对道路场景图像多边形语义分割标注耗时费力的问题，提出了开源本地桌面标注工具RoadAnnoter v1.0。该工具集成了手动标注、SAM/MobileSAM交互分割、边缘填充、SegFormer通用预训练分割以及可基于累积标注进行迭代训练的轻量化TinySegNet共六种人机协同模式，并配有统一的掩膜转多边形流水线和YOLO导出支持。在实际道路场景数据集构建中展现了良好的几何适应性与标注便利性。
AI.keywords: RoadAnnoter, 语义分割标注, 人机协同, 道路场景, 交互式分割
AI.comments: 该工具将基础分割模型（SAM/MobileSAM）、预训练模型（SegFormer）、轻量级自适应微调网络（TinySegNet）与传统CV算法（Canny边缘检测与泛洪填充）集成在本地桌面端，实用性强且保护数据隐私。局限在于摘要中明确指出尚未进行定量准确性评估，仅依赖定性分析与对比。

title: The Whole Warps the Parts: Attentional Certainty Modulates Ensemble-Induced Bias in Visualizations
summary: Data visualizations often require viewers to extract both ensemble statistics and individual values from collections of graphical marks. Yet individual items embedded within an ensemble can be systematically biased by that context. Prior studies have reported both repulsion away from and attraction toward ensemble statistics, but these effects have been observed across different conditions. We test whether task or attentional certainty explains these opposing forms of ensemble-induced bias. In Study 1, observers briefly viewed ensembles of differently sized circles and then judged the size of an individual circle embedded within the ensemble. Using a common stimulus generation framework, we tested both identification and discrimination when the target was specified before or after the ensemble, and an additional no-cue identification condition without a specified target. Under the shared cued conditions, effects were predominantly repulsive or near zero in both identification and discrimination. In contrast, eliminating target-specific information reversed ensemble-induced bias from repulsion to attraction. Identification precision also decreased systematically from pre-cue to post-cue to no-cue conditions. Study 2 replicated this cue-dependent pattern in graphical displays of startup valuations and precinct vote contributions. Our findings isolate attentional certainty as a key determinant of whether ensemble context repels or attracts individual-item representations, extending the design question beyond precision to how attention directing choices determine which bias the viewer will be operating under.

AI.title_translation: 整体扭曲局部：注意确定性调节可视化中由整体引起的知觉偏差
AI.tldr: 研究发现注意确定性决定了整体环境对局部项估计是产生“排斥”还是“吸引”偏差，为图表设计中的注意力引导提供了新依据。
AI.motivation: 在数据可视化中，整体环境常常系统性地扭曲局部项的估计，但以往研究在不同条件下分别观察到了局部向整体统计值“吸引”或被其“排斥”的矛盾现象。本研究旨在探究任务类型或注意确定性是否能解释这种相反的整体诱发偏差。
AI.method: 研究包含两个实验：研究1采用大小不一的圆形刺激集合，通过前线索（pre-cue）、后线索（post-cue）和无目标线索（no-cue）操纵注意确定性，测试被试在识别和辨别任务中对特定圆大小的判断；研究2将该范式复制并推广到初创公司估值和选区投票贡献的实际数据可视化图表中。
AI.result: 在线索提示条件下（前线索和后线索），被试在识别和辨别任务中主要表现出排斥效应或近零偏差；而在消除目标特异性信息的无提示条件下，整体诱发的偏差由排斥逆转为吸引。同时，识别精度从前线索到后线索再到无提示呈系统性下降。研究2在实际图表场景中成功复现了这一依赖于线索的模式。
AI.conclusion: 注意确定性是决定整体背景对单个项目表征产生排斥还是吸引偏差的关键决定因素；图表设计不仅要考虑感知精度，还需关注注意力引导方式如何决定用户所受偏差的类型。
AI.translation: 数据可视化通常要求观察者从图形标记集合中同时提取整体统计信息与单个数值。然而，嵌入在整体中的单个项目可能会被其所处的上下文系统性地产生知觉偏差。以往研究分别报道了远离整体统计值的排斥效应和朝向整体统计值的吸引效应，但这些效应是在不同条件下观察到的。我们测试了任务类型或注意确定性是否能解释这些形式相反的整体诱发偏差。在研究1中，观察者短暂浏览大小不一的圆形集合，然后判断集合中某个圆的大小。在一个通用的刺激生成框架下，我们测试了在整体呈现之前或之后指定目标时的识别与辨别任务，以及未指定目标的无提示识别任务。在相同的有提示条件下，识别和辨别中的效应主要表现为排斥或接近于零。相反，消除目标特异性信息后，整体诱发的偏差从排斥逆转为吸引。识别精度也从前提示、后提示到无提示条件系统性地下降。研究2在初创公司估值和选区投票贡献的图形展示中复现了这种依赖于提示的模式。我们的研究结果明确了注意确定性是决定整体背景排斥还是吸引单个项目表征的关键因素，将可视化设计问题从单纯的精度考量延伸至注意引导策略如何决定观察者所面临的偏差类型。
AI.summary: 本研究探讨了注意确定性对数据可视化中整体诱发偏差（吸引与排斥）的调节作用。实验表明，在线索明确的条件下，个体估计倾向于被整体统计特征排斥；而在线索缺失、注意确定性降低时，偏差逆转为吸引，且识别精度随确定性降低而下降。该结论揭示了注意力引导机制对图表感知偏差性质的深层影响。
AI.keywords: 数据可视化, 整体偏差, 注意确定性, 排斥与吸引效应, 知觉扭曲
AI.comments: 该研究的重要创新在于统一并解释了以往研究中整体背景对局部估计产生“排斥”与“吸引”这一对立现象的矛盾，证明注意确定性是决定偏差方向的关键变量。其重要性在于将可视化评估从单纯的“读图精度”拓展到了“知觉偏差方向”的层面，对如何通过提示或高亮等注意力引导手段优化图表设计具有重要指导意义。局限性在于测试主要集中在静态简单标记和二维气泡图/散点图式场景，未来需在更复杂、多变量或动态交互的可视化中进一步验证。

title: Stopping Is Not the Limit: Understanding and Eliciting Agent Capability in Long-Horizon Vulnerability Exploitation
summary: Vulnerability exploitation tests whether language model agents can develop working exploits from known software flaws. Sequential test-time scaling can improve exploitation performance, but larger budgets do not ensure sustained exploration: agents often stop with budget remaining. Yet what happens when execution continues beyond stopping remains underexplored. We investigate this gap on ExploitBench using DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 and MiMo-V2.6-Pro. We find additional verified gains after the first stop response, but gains diminish over longer execution. We identify two patterns associated with less productive continuation: an increasing proportion of stop responses within the same context and earlier stopping associated with summaries retaining impossibility judgments about unachieved capabilities. To test whether context management can elicit further capability, we propose SCoRe, which compacts context at stop bursts and marks these judgments as unproven. SCoRe improves verified capability over summary-based continuation and other evaluated context-management baselines. With SCoRe, MiMo reaches a capability coverage score of 67.0% at 2,000 turns, exceeding both 32.4% under the original stopping policy and the 58.6% computed for GPT-5.5 from ExploitBench's 300-turn reference results on the same tasks. These findings show that stopping need not mark an agent's exploitation limit, and that continued execution with context management can elicit substantial further capability.

AI.title_translation: 停止并非终点：理解与激发智能体在长程漏洞利用中的能力
AI.tldr: 论文发现LLM智能体在漏洞利用任务中提前停止并不等于达到能力上限，通过提出的SCoRe上下文管理策略纠正错误停滞判定，可大幅提升智能体的长程利用能力。
AI.motivation: 在漏洞利用任务中，顺序测试时扩展（test-time scaling）虽能提升性能，但更大的预算无法保证持续探索，智能体往往在预算未耗尽时就提前停止，而停止之后继续执行会带来何种影响目前尚未得到深入探究。
AI.method: 在ExploitBench基准上评估模型（DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731和MiMo-V2.6-Pro）在首次停止后的表现，分析导致低效延续的模式（同上下文内停止响应比例增加、摘要中保留未达成能力的‘不可能’判定）。进而提出SCoRe方法，在停止爆发点压缩上下文，并将既有的‘不可能’判定标记为‘未被证实’，以此打破探索僵局。
AI.result: 首次停止后继续执行能带来经检验的额外增益，但增益会随执行增长而递减；SCoRe在经检验能力上优于基于摘要的延续策略及其他基线。在2000轮交互下，MiMo结合SCoRe使能力覆盖得分达到67.0%，远超原始停止策略下的32.4%，并超越了同任务下GPT-5.5在300轮参考结果中的58.6%。
AI.conclusion: 智能体的主动停止并不代表其能力极限；在停止后通过有效的上下文管理继续执行，可以充分激发智能体更深层次的漏洞利用能力。
AI.translation: 漏洞利用旨在测试语言模型智能体是否能根据已知软件缺陷构建出可行的利用程序。顺序测试时扩展可以提高漏洞利用性能，但更大的计算预算并不一定能保证持续的探索：智能体通常会在预算尚有剩余时就停止。然而，当执行超越停止点继续进行时会发生什么，目前仍缺乏充分研究。我们在ExploitBench上使用DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731和MiMo-V2.6-Pro对这一空白进行了调查。我们发现，在首次给出停止响应之后仍可获得经验证的额外增益，但随着执行时间的延长，增益会出现递减。我们指出了与低效延续相关的两种模式：同一上下文中停止响应的比例不断增加，以及摘要中保留了对未实现能力的“不可能”判断从而导致提前停止。为了测试上下文管理是否能激发更多能力，我们提出了SCoRe，该方法在停止集中爆发时压缩上下文，并将这些不可能判断标记为“未被证实”。相比于基于摘要的延续策略及其他评估的上下文管理基线，SCoRe提升了经验证的能力。借助SCoRe，MiMo在2,000轮次时的能力覆盖得分达到67.0%，既超过了原始停止策略下的32.4%，也超过了相同任务下ExploitBench 300轮参考结果中为GPT-5.5计算出的58.6%。这些发现表明，停止并不必然标志着智能体的漏洞利用能力极限，通过上下文管理继续执行可以激发巨大的潜在能力。
AI.summary: 本研究探索了语言模型智能体在长程漏洞利用中提前停止后的行为表现。研究发现智能体会过早停止且摘要中的否定判断阻碍后续探索。为此提出SCoRe上下文管理方法，在停止密集时压缩上下文并将失败判定重设为未被证实，从而大幅提升了长程任务中的能力覆盖率和漏洞利用效果。
AI.keywords: 漏洞利用, 语言模型智能体, 测试时扩展, 上下文管理, 长程探索
AI.comments: 该研究敏锐地抓住了长程智能体任务中‘过早停止（premature stopping）’这一核心痛点，指出了模型由于上下文记忆中的‘不可能判断’而产生探索停滞的机制。所提出的SCoRe方法通过上下文压缩和纠正确定性认知，有效释放了模型的潜在探索能力，对提升长上下文/复杂决策场景下的Agent推理能力具有重要的启发意义。

title: Beyond Attribute-Centric Fairness: Modelling and Mitigating Unified Bias Representation in Omni-modal Large Language Models
summary: Omni-modal large language models (OLLMs) provide joint multimodal understanding and generation capabilities, making them well-suited to complex environments and promising backbones for next-generation AI. Despite these advances, the harmful stereotypes encoded in such models manifest in increasingly diverse forms, leading to broader and more severe societal consequences. Existing debiasing methods typically impose separate fairness objectives for each sensitive attribute and modality to minimise demographic-dependent variations. However, in omni-modal settings, this attribute-centric paradigm struggles to jointly address diverse social biases with distinct fairness objectives and to generalise beyond predefined attributes. To this end, we propose OmniDebias, one of the first methods for promoting fairness in OLLMs, which employs a bias-centric formulation to extract and mitigate a shared bias representation across attributes and modalities while preserving attribute-related knowledge. Specifically, we exploit activation inconsistencies of a given attribute (e.g., gender) across semantic contexts (e.g., occupations) to disentangle bias from legitimate knowledge. We further consolidate multiple extracted biases into a shared representation, formulating a unified objective that captures the underlying structure across social biases and generalises to unseen attributes. Extensive experiments demonstrate that eliminating unified bias with both post-hoc editing and fine-tuning can consistently improve fairness across diverse attributes and modalities in OLLMs while maintaining favourable utility.

AI.title_translation: 超越以属性为中心的公平性：在全模态大语言模型中建模与缓解统一偏见表征
AI.tldr: 针对全模态大模型难以兼顾多属性与跨模态去偏的问题，本文提出OmniDebias，通过解耦偏见与有效知识并构建统一共享偏见表示，实现了跨模态、可泛化的公平性提升且不损模型效用。
AI.motivation: 全模态大语言模型中编码的刻板印象形式愈发多样。现有的去偏方法多针对特定敏感属性和特定模态设置独立的公平性目标（以属性为中心），难以在全模态场景下协同处理多类社会偏见，且无法泛化至未预先定义的属性。
AI.method: 提出OmniDebias方法，采用“以偏见为中心”的构想：1）利用特定属性在不同语义上下文中的激活不一致性，将有害偏见与合法属性知识解耦；2）将提取出的多种偏见整合为跨属性与跨模态的共享统一偏见表示；3）构建统一优化目标，支持通过事后编辑（post-hoc editing）或微调（fine-tuning）来消除该统一偏见。
AI.result: 大量实验表明，在后处理模型编辑和微调中消除该统一偏见表示，能够持续提升OLLM在多种属性与模态上的公平性，并保持良好的模型实用效用。
AI.conclusion: OmniDebias通过建模统一偏见表示并在后处理编辑与微调中予以消除，能够有效提升全模态大语言模型在多模态与多属性上的公平性，并具备向未知属性泛化的能力，同时兼顾了模型原有的效用。
AI.translation: 全模态大语言模型（OLLM）具备联合的多模态理解与生成能力，使其非常适合复杂环境，并成为下一代人工智能的有前景的基座。尽管取得了这些进展，但此类模型中编码的有害刻板印象表现出日益多样的形式，导致了更广泛且更严重的社会后果。现有的去偏方法通常针对每个敏感属性和模态施加单独的公平性目标，以最小化依赖人口统计学特征的差异。然而，在全模态环境中，这种以属性为中心的范式难以通过各异的公平性目标协同解决多样化的社会偏见，也难以泛化到预定义属性之外。为此，我们提出了OmniDebias，这是首批促进OLLM公平性的方法之一，它采用以偏见为中心的表述，提取并缓解跨属性和模态的共享偏见表示，同时保留与属性相关的知识。具体而言，我们利用给定属性（如性别）在不同语义上下文（如职业）中的激活不一致性，将偏见与合理知识解耦。我们进一步将提取出的多种偏见整合为一个共享表示，构建了一个能够捕捉跨社会偏见的底层结构并可泛化至未见属性的统一目标。大量实验表明，通过事后编辑和微调来消除统一偏见，可以在保持良好实用性的同时，持续提升OLLM在多样化属性和模态下的公平性。
AI.summary: 本文针对全模态大语言模型（OLLM）中存在的刻板印象与偏见问题，指出传统“以属性为中心”去偏方法的局限性，提出了首批针对OLLM的去偏方法之一OmniDebias。该方法基于“以偏见为中心”的范式，通过语义上下文激活不一致性解耦合法知识与偏见，并构建跨模态与跨属性的统一共享偏见表示。实验证明，该方法在事后编辑和微调中均能显著提升跨模态与属性的公平性，且能泛化至未见属性并维持良好的实用效能。
AI.keywords: 全模态大语言模型, 偏见消除, 属性偏见, 统一偏见表示, 模型公平性
AI.comments: 该研究创新性地突破了传统的“以属性为中心”的去偏偏见范式，针对全模态大语言模型（OLLM）提出了“以偏见为中心”的统一表示建模方法。其重要性在于能够跨模态、跨属性捕获共享偏见结构，并泛化至未预定义的属性，同时保留了模型的实用性与合法知识。局限在于摘要中未明确说明该方法在极端多模态或全新模态（如音频、视频等多源异构输入）下的计算开销与性能边界。

title: Wear and Go: Calibration Free Sparse Inertial Motion Capture via Online Sensor Setup Estimation
summary: Sparse inertial motion capture typically assumes that each sensor's anatomical identity and mounting orientation are known. We present MOSAIC (Motion-based Sensor Assignment and Inertial Calibration), a framework that recovers this setup from ordinary motion without a calibration pose. Our central insight is that body pose changes continuously while the sensor setup persists, allowing movements that are individually ambiguous to provide complementary evidence over time. A setup network processes unordered sensor streams with temporal and cross-sensor attention, then accumulates assignment and rotation evidence into a session-level estimate. The recovered setup canonicalizes measurements for frozen pretrained pose estimators, separating sensor configuration from motion reconstruction. For sensors worn at prescribed body sites, evaluation on real inertial recordings with randomized setups shows near-calibrated pose accuracy for bounded offsets and substantial benefits from accumulation under arbitrary orientations. Transfer across pose networks supports setup recovery as a reusable interface between interchangeable sensors and pretrained pose models.

AI.title_translation: 即戴即用：基于在线传感器配置估计的免标定稀疏惯性动作捕捉
AI.tldr: 提出MOSAIC框架，无需标定姿势，仅通过普通运动在线推断无序传感器的佩戴部位与朝向，实现免标定的稀疏惯性动作捕捉。
AI.motivation: 传统的稀疏惯性动作捕捉依赖预先已知的传感器解剖学身份（佩戴部位）与安装朝向，通常需要用户做出特定的标定姿势，使用体验繁琐且限制了便捷性。
AI.method: 提出MOSAIC框架，利用身体姿态持续变化而传感器配置固定的特性，使用结合时序与跨传感器注意力机制的网络处理无序传感器流，将各时刻的部位分配与旋转证据累积为会话级配置估计，并将数据规范化后输入冻结的预训练姿态估计器中。
AI.result: 在具有随机配置的真实惯性数据评估中，对于预定部位的传感器，在有界偏移下取得了接近标定水准的姿态估计精度；在任意朝向下时序累积机制优势显著，并展现了在不同姿态网络间的良好迁移能力。
AI.conclusion: MOSAIC证明了无需特定标定姿势，仅凭自然日常运动即可在线准确估计传感器的分配与朝向，可作为通用、可互换的接口赋能各类预训练惯性姿态估计模型。
AI.translation: 稀疏惯性动作捕捉通常假设每个传感器的解剖学身份和安装朝向是已知的。我们提出了MOSAIC（基于运动的传感器分配与惯性标定），这是一个无需标定姿势、直接从日常运动中恢复该配置的框架。我们的核心洞见在于：身体姿态是连续变化的，而传感器配置保持稳定，从而使原本单帧下具有歧义的运动能够随时间提供互补证据。配置网络利用时序与跨传感器注意力处理无序的传感器数据流，随后将分配和旋转证据累积为会话级别的估计。恢复出的配置可规范化测量数据并输入到冻结的预训练姿态估计器中，从而将传感器配置与动作重建解耦。对于佩戴在预定身体部位的传感器，在带有随机配置的真实惯性记录上的评估表明，在有界偏移下其姿态精度接近已标定状态，且在任意朝向下时序累积带来了显著增益。在不同姿态网络间的迁移能力，支持将配置恢复作为可互换传感器与预训练姿态模型之间的可复用接口。
AI.summary: 本研究提出了免标定稀疏惯性动作捕捉框架MOSAIC。该方法利用自然运动在时间维度上的互补信息，通过时序与跨传感器注意力网络在线估计无序传感器的身份与朝向，规范化输入并与姿态重建解耦，实现了无需标定姿态的即戴即用惯性动捕。
AI.keywords: 稀疏惯性动捕, 免标定, 传感器配置估计, 姿态重建, 注意力机制
AI.comments: 该论文创新性地摆脱了传统惯性动作捕捉对特定标定姿态（如T-pose）的依赖，提出了“即戴即用”的范式；通过将传感器配置估计与姿态重建解耦，使其具备高度模块化和可迁移性。局限在于目前实验仍然假定传感器佩戴在预定的解剖学身体部位集合中，对于非预定部位的泛化能力仍待进一步探索。

title: Impact of Pretraining Length, Model Size, and Annotation Budget on Downstream Clinical Tasks of Foundation Models in Radiotherapy
comments: 9 pages, 5 figures, 2 tables. Supplementary Material included
summary: Cone-beam CT (CBCT) scans acquired during radiotherapy capture changes such as tumor shrinkage and radiation-induced tissue changes, offering great potential for foundation models that help monitor individual treatment responses. However, to our knowledge, no large-scale pretrained models for radiotherapy CBCT exist, and evaluating modeling choices is difficult since downstream tasks are not known in advance. We examine how pretraining length, model size, and finetuning strategy relate to downstream clinical performance, and how metrics tracked during pretraining correlate with it. We pretrain vision transformer encoders with masked image modeling on about 150,000 raw 3D radiotherapy CBCT scans, tracking representation quality via validation loss, effective rank, and linear probing. Downstream tasks are classification of feeding tube presence ($n=51,135$ CBCTs, $1,562$ patients) and clinical characteristics (T-, N-stage, sex, age, tumor site; $n=1,278$ patients) in head and neck cancer. We compare low-rank adaptation (LoRA) and full finetuning against no pretraining, varying annotated dataset size. Pretext validation loss was the most consistent predictor of downstream performance; effective rank and linear probing were also associated, but not consistently across model sizes and finetuning methods. LoRA performed comparably to full finetuning while training only 0.5-2.5% of the parameters. Fully finetuned models consistently outperformed models without pretraining across all sizes, with AUROC 0.91-0.97 vs. 0.58-0.85 for feeding tube classification and 0.99-1.00 vs. 0.71-0.97 for sex classification. Model size had only a small, inconsistent effect, suggesting smaller models suffice at lower computational cost. Code and pretrained models (non-commercial license): https://github.com/alexCortinaU/RT-CBCT_SSL
comment: 9 pages, 5 figures, 2 tables. Supplementary Material included

AI.title_translation: 预训练时长、模型大小和标注预算对放疗基础模型下游临床任务的影响
AI.tldr: 研究在15万例放疗CBCT上训练了首个3D基础模型，证明预训练可大幅提升临床下游任务性能，且轻量ViT结合LoRA即可达到顶尖效果。
AI.motivation: 放疗中的锥形束CT（CBCT）能够追踪肿瘤及组织的动态变化，具备构建基础模型的巨大潜力，但目前尚无针对放疗CBCT的大规模预训练模型，且在下游任务未知的情况下难以有效评估预训练和建模方案的选择。
AI.method: 基于掩码图像建模（MIM）在约15万例放疗3D CBCT原始扫描上预训练视觉Transformer（ViT）编码器；在预训练过程中通过验证损失、有效秩和线性探测跟踪表征质量；在头颈癌鼻饲管分类及多项临床特征预测下游任务中，对比了LoRA微调、全参数微调与从头训练在不同标注量下的表现。
AI.result: 预训练验证损失是下游表现最稳定一致的预测指标；LoRA微调仅需更新0.5%-2.5%的参数即可取得与全参数微调相当的表现；预训练模型显著优于无预训练模型（鼻饲管分类AUROC 0.91-0.97 vs. 0.58-0.85，性别分类 0.99-1.00 vs. 0.71-0.97）；模型尺寸对性能影响较小且不一致，轻量模型即可满足需求。
AI.conclusion: 自监督预训练显著提升了CBCT下游临床任务的预测性能；预训练验证损失是预测下游效果的最佳代理指标；结合小模型与LoRA微调能够在极低计算资源下实现高精度的临床任务预测。
AI.translation: 放射治疗期间采集的锥形束CT（CBCT）扫描能够记录肿瘤缩小以及辐射引起的组织变化等，在构建协助监测个体治疗反应的基础模型方面蕴含巨大潜力。然而，据我们所知，目前尚不存在针对放疗CBCT的大规模预训练模型，且在下游任务未知的情况下评估建模选择较为困难。我们研究了预训练时长、模型大小和微调策略与下游临床性能之间的关系，以及预训练阶段追踪的指标与下游性能的相关性。我们在约150,000例放疗3D CBCT原始扫描上，使用掩码图像建模预训练了视觉Transformer编码器，并通过验证损失、有效秩和线性探测评估表征质量。下游任务为头颈癌患者的鼻饲管存在性分类（n=51,135例CBCT，1,562位患者）和临床特征分类（T分期、N分期、性别、年龄、肿瘤部位；n=1,278位患者）。我们通过改变标注数据集大小，对比了低秩自适应（LoRA）、全参数微调与从头训练的表现。前置任务验证损失是下游性能最一致的预测指标；有效秩和线性探测也具有相关性，但在不同模型尺寸和微调方法间表现并不一致。LoRA仅训练0.5%-2.5%的参数便取得了与全参数微调相当的性能。全微调模型在所有尺寸下均显著优于无预训练模型，鼻饲管分类的AUROC达到0.91-0.97（对比0.58-0.85），性别分类达到0.99-1.00（对比0.71-0.97）。模型尺寸的影响较小且不一致，表明较小的模型即可在更低的计算成本下满足需求。代码和预训练模型（非商业许可）开源于：https://github.com/alexCortinaU/RT-CBCT_SSL。
AI.summary: 本研究针对放疗3D CBCT数据构建了基于15万例扫描的自监督基础模型，系统探讨了预训练时长、模型尺寸、微调策略（LoRA对比全参数微调）和标注数据量对头颈癌下游临床任务的影响，证实了预训练的必要性以及轻量模型与高效微调方案的优越性。
AI.keywords: 锥形束CT (CBCT), 基础模型, 自监督学习, 放射治疗, 低秩自适应 (LoRA)
AI.comments: 该论文填补了放疗CBCT领域缺乏大规模自监督基础模型的空白，具有很强的临床实用价值。其系统性评估了预训练监控指标与下游性能的相关性，并证实了参数高效微调（LoRA）与轻量化ViT模型在医疗影像落地中的可行性与高性价比，为资源受限场景下的放疗AI开发提供了重要依据。

title: Born for the Task: Rethinking Quantum Chemistry with Foresighted Agentic Computing
summary: Quantum chemistry relies on general-purpose software, whose generality leaves many large-scale calculations beyond practical resource budgets. Coding agents make task-specific programs cheap to write, but not efficient ones easy to find: whether a computational strategy is accurate and fast enough becomes clear only after it actually runs at the target scale. We introduce BORN, a foresighted agentic computing framework that synthesizes high performance quantum chemistry programs on demand. BORN anticipates the behavior of each strategy before execution, extrapolating its error from representative small systems and predicting its runtime from the target-scale workload and measured hardware throughputs. Building on these predictions, BORN unfolds the preset schemes of existing packages into independently configurable algorithmic components, selects the fastest strategy within the error tolerance from the predicted accuracy-runtime Pareto frontier, and guides coding agents to compile it with component-level performance predictions. For a Hartree-Fock calculation with 50,024 basis functions, BORN finishes in 1.41h on a single CPU node, 77$\times$ faster than the estimated runtime of a general-purpose baseline and still 9.8$\times$ faster with development time included. On a single GPU, BORN completes the ubiquitin calculation in 2.1,h, the same order of runtime as the GPU-accelerated package Mako on 64 GPUs, and shortens the B-DNA duplex calculation from an estimated two months to 8.1,h (173$\times$).

AI.title_translation: 为任务而生：通过前瞻性智能体计算重新思考量子化学
AI.tldr: BORN是一个结合了事前误差与耗时预测的前瞻性智能体计算框架，能按需自动合成专用量子化学程序，实现超百倍的计算加速。
AI.motivation: 通用量子化学软件因其通用性难以在实际资源预算内完成大规模计算；而代码智能体虽易于编写专用程序，却无法在目标规模实际运行前预知该策略是否具备足够的精度与速度。
AI.method: 提出前瞻性智能体计算框架BORN：1）在执行前从小系统推演误差，结合目标规模工作负载和实测硬件吞吐量预测策略耗时；2）将现有软件包的方案解构为可独立配置的算法组件，从预测的精度-耗时帕累托前沿中选取满足误差容限的最优策略；3）基于组件级性能预测引导编程智能体按需编译并生成高效程序。
AI.result: 在50,024个基函数的Hartree-Fock计算中，单CPU节点耗时1.41小时，比通用基线估计快77倍（含开发时间快9.8倍）；在单GPU上，泛素计算耗时2.1小时（达到GPU加速包Mako在64卡上的耗时量级），并将B-DNA双链计算从预计的2个月缩短至8.1小时（加速173倍）。
AI.conclusion: BORN通过前瞻性性能与精度预测指导智能体按需合成专用程序，成功突破了传统通用量子化学软件在大规模计算中的资源与耗时瓶颈。
AI.translation: 量子化学依赖于通用软件，但其通用性使得许多大规模计算超出了实际的资源预算。编程智能体虽然降低了编写任务特定程序的成本，但要找到高效程序并不容易：一种计算策略是否足够精确和快速，往往只有在它实际于目标规模下运行后才能明朗。我们提出了BORN，一个前瞻性智能体计算框架，可按需合成高性能量子化学程序。BORN在执行前预判每种策略的表现，从小规模代表性系统中推演其误差，并根据目标规模的工作负载与实测硬件吞吐量预测其运行时间。基于这些预测，BORN将现有软件包的预设方案解构为可独立配置的算法组件，从预测的精度-耗时帕累托前沿中选择误差容限内最快的策略，并通过组件级性能预测指导编程智能体完成编译。对于包含50,024个基函数的Hartree-Fock计算，BORN在单CPU节点上耗时1.41小时完成，比通用基准的预估运行时间快77倍，即使计入开发时间仍快9.8倍。在单GPU上，BORN在2.1小时内完成了泛素计算，与GPU加速软件包Mako在64块GPU上的运行时间处于同一量级，并将B-DNA双螺旋计算从预计的两个月缩短至8.1小时（加速173倍）。
AI.summary: 本文提出了BORN框架，该框架能够在实际执行前外推误差并预测耗时，解构算法组件并选取最优帕累托策略，进而指导代码智能体按需合成高性能专用量子化学程序，大幅降低了大规模体系计算的时间和硬件成本。
AI.keywords: 量子化学, 智能体计算, 程序合成, 性能预测, 帕累托前沿
AI.comments: 该研究创新性地将性能/误差前瞻预测机制与代码生成智能体相结合，解决了在未实际运行前难以评估定制程序在大规模任务下精度与效率的核心痛点。实验表明其在单CPU/单GPU上的表现可匹敌甚至大幅超越传统集群计算，对AI for Science中特定科学计算软件的自动化、高性能定制具有重要的应用价值。

title: You Only Encode Once: Sub-Pixel-Shifted Frames for Arbitrary-Scale Remote Sensing Super-Resolution with 2D Gaussian Splatting
summary: Arbitrary-scale super-resolution (ASSR) of remote sensing images remains challenging due to the limited high-frequency information in a single low-resolution (LR) observation. While multi-frame SR can exploit complementary sub-pixel information, existing approaches often require real multi-frame training sequences and repeated feature encoding, increasing data acquisition demands and computational costs. To address these limitations, we propose SPS-GS (Sub-Pixel-Shifted Gaussian Splatting), an encode-once framework that learns from multi-phase LR observations synthesized from individual high-resolution images, without requiring real multi-frame training sequences. Specifically, Phase-Coherent Aliasing Demodulation (PCAD) exploits shift-dependent aliasing through Fourier-based alignment, phase-aware residual fusion, and least-squares aliasing estimation, enabling multi-frame information to be integrated before a single deep encoding pass. Gaussian Projection Alignment (GPA) then iteratively refines Gaussian centers and colors using multi-observation back-projection to promote observation consistency. The refined Gaussians support continuous rendering at arbitrary scales. Extensive experiments on five remote sensing datasets demonstrate strong reconstruction performance against single-image and multi-frame SR baselines, while maintaining competitive inference efficiency at common scales. The code will be publicly released.

AI.title_translation: 你只编码一次：结合2D高斯泼溅的亚像素偏移帧用于任意尺度遥感超分辨率
AI.tldr: 该论文提出了SPS-GS，一个用于遥感图像任意尺度超分辨率的一次编码框架，它通过合成亚像素偏移的低分辨率观测和2D高斯泼溅来解决现有方法的局限性，实现了卓越的重建性能和效率。
AI.motivation: 遥感图像的任意尺度超分辨率（ASSR）面临挑战，因为单个低分辨率（LR）观测中的高频信息有限。现有的多帧超分辨率方法需要真实的多帧训练序列和重复的特征编码，这导致数据采集需求和计算成本增加。
AI.method: 本文提出了SPS-GS（亚像素偏移高斯泼溅），一个一次编码的框架，它从由单个高分辨率图像合成的多相LR观测中学习，无需真实的多帧训练序列。具体而言，相位相干混叠解调（PCAD）通过基于傅里叶的对齐、相位感知残差融合和最小二乘混叠估计来利用与位移相关的混叠，从而在单个深度编码过程之前整合多帧信息。随后，高斯投影对齐（GPA）利用多观测反向投影迭代地细化高斯中心和颜色，以促进观测一致性。细化后的高斯支持任意尺度的连续渲染。
AI.result: 在五个遥感数据集上进行的广泛实验表明，与单幅图像和多帧超分辨率基线相比，SPS-GS表现出强大的重建性能，同时在常见尺度下保持了具有竞争力的推理效率。
AI.conclusion: SPS-GS通过利用合成的多相低分辨率观测和一次编码框架，有效解决了遥感图像任意尺度超分辨率的挑战，实现了强大的性能和效率。
AI.translation: 遥感图像的任意尺度超分辨率（ASSR）仍然具有挑战性，原因在于单个低分辨率（LR）观测中高频信息有限。尽管多帧超分辨率可以利用互补的亚像素信息，但现有方法通常需要真实的多帧训练序列和重复的特征编码，这增加了数据采集需求和计算成本。为了解决这些限制，我们提出了SPS-GS（亚像素偏移高斯泼溅），这是一个一次编码的框架，它从由单个高分辨率图像合成的多相LR观测中学习，而无需真实的多帧训练序列。具体来说，相位相干混叠解调（PCAD）通过基于傅里叶的对齐、相位感知残差融合和最小二乘混叠估计来利用与位移相关的混叠，从而实现在单个深度编码过程之前整合多帧信息。然后，高斯投影对齐（GPA）使用多观测反向投影迭代地细化高斯中心和颜色，以促进观测一致性。细化后的高斯支持任意尺度的连续渲染。在五个遥感数据集上进行的广泛实验表明，与单幅图像和多帧超分辨率基线相比，该方法表现出强大的重建性能，同时在常见尺度下保持了具有竞争力的推理效率。代码将公开发布。
AI.summary: 该论文介绍了SPS-GS，一个用于遥感图像任意尺度超分辨率的一次编码框架。它通过从合成的亚像素偏移低分辨率观测中学习，而不是依赖真实的多帧序列，解决了现有多帧超分辨率方法的局限性。该框架采用相位相干混叠解调（PCAD）高效整合多帧信息，并利用高斯投影对齐（GPA）细化高斯以实现连续的任意尺度渲染。实验结果表明，在遥感数据集上，SPS-GS展现出卓越的重建性能和具有竞争力的效率。
AI.keywords: 任意尺度超分辨率, 遥感, 多帧超分辨率, 高斯泼溅, 一次编码
AI.comments: 该论文的创新之处在于其“一次编码”框架，通过利用合成的多相低分辨率观测，避免了对真实多帧训练数据和重复编码的需求。将PCAD和GPA与2D高斯泼溅结合以实现任意尺度渲染，是一种新颖的方法。这项工作对于解决遥感图像处理中的关键挑战具有重要意义，为高质量图像放大提供了一种更数据高效和计算有效的方法。

title: A Dichotomy for Exact Quantum Circuit Amplitudes
summary: We classify the complexity of exactly computing computational-basis amplitudes for circuits over any fixed finite library of unitary qubit gates, with each gate allowed to act on any ordered tuple of distinct wires. Exact evaluation is polynomial-time computable if all gates permute the computational basis up to phases, all preserve product states, or all become Clifford under a common diagonal one-qubit unitary change of basis on every wire. For every other library, the problem is $\#\mathrm P$-hard under polynomial-time Turing reductions. Our proof connects circuit amplitudes to the Boolean Holant classification of tensor contractions on arbitrary graphs. For an algebraic library containing a nonmonomial gate and an entangling gate, we show how to simulate the joint use of a symmetric maximally entangled state and its adjoint at polynomial cost, using only amplitude queries over the original library. This lets us evaluate unrestricted contractions of the resulting gate and boundary tensors. Unitarity and the computational-basis boundaries then restrict the tractable cases to the three forms above. Algebraic specialization extends the dichotomy to arbitrary fixed complex gate entries under a symbolic exact-output convention.

title: blaris: Windowless Random-Access LZSS for Constrained Microcontrollers
comments: 4 pages, 1 figure, 2 tables. Source code and benchmark suite available at https://github.com/lis05/blaris
summary: Embedded LZ77 decompressors (such as heatshrink and tamp) require an in-RAM sliding window that couples memory usage to compression ratio and incurs high latency on random-access reads. We present blaris, a lightweight, windowless LZSS decompressor for execute-in-place (XIP) random access on constrained microcontrollers. By partitioning tokens into bidirectionally traversable streams with power-of-two checkpoints, blaris resolves back-references directly in the compressed payload, achieving compression ratios comparable to high-window heatshrink and tamp configurations without allocating a RAM window. Targeting compress-on-host, decompress-on-device workflows, blaris assumes trusted build-time payloads and omits runtime error and bounds checks. On RV32IMC, it requires just 548-784 B of Flash and 104-112 B of total RAM, achieving orders-of-magnitude faster small-slice random reads than ratio-matched, block-indexed heatshrink and tamp.
comment: 4 pages, 1 figure, 2 tables. Source code and benchmark suite available at https://github.com/lis05/blaris

AI.title_translation: blaris：面向受限微控制器的无滑动窗口可随机访问LZSS解压缩器
AI.tldr: blaris是一种专为受限微控制器设计的无RAM滑动窗口LZSS解压缩器，可在极低内存占用下实现出色的压缩率和极速的XIP随机读取。
AI.motivation: 现有的嵌入式LZ77解压缩器（如heatshrink和tamp）需要片上RAM滑动窗口，导致内存占用与压缩率耦合，并在执行随机访问读取时产生较高的延迟。
AI.method: 提出了轻量级无窗口解压器blaris：1) 将tokens划分为带有2的幂次检查点（power-of-two checkpoints）的双向可遍历流，直接在压缩数据中解析反向引用，无需在RAM中分配滑动窗口；2) 面向主机端压缩、设备端解压的流程，假设数据可信从而去除了运行时的错误与边界检查。
AI.result: 在RV32IMC架构上，blaris仅占用548-784字节的Flash和104-112字节的RAM；其压缩率与采用大窗口配置的heatshrink及tamp相当；在小切片随机读取速度上，比同等压缩率且采用分块索引的heatshrink和tamp快数个数量级。
AI.conclusion: blaris成功实现了一种无RAM滑动窗口的轻量级LZSS解压器，在资源受限微控制器上以极低的Flash和RAM开销，提供了与主流算法匹敌的压缩率以及快数个数量级的随机访问性能。
AI.translation: 嵌入式LZ77解压缩器（例如heatshrink和tamp）需要占用RAM的滑动窗口，这使得内存占用与压缩率强相关，并在随机访问读取时导致较高的延迟。我们提出了blaris，这是一种轻量级、无滑动窗口的LZSS解压缩器，适用于受限微控制器上的就地执行（XIP）随机访问。通过将标记（token）划分为带有2的幂次检查点的双向可遍历流，blaris能够直接在压缩有效负载中解析后向引用，从而在不分配RAM窗口的情况下，获得了与大窗口配置下的heatshrink和tamp相当的压缩率。blaris针对主机端压缩、设备端解压的工作流程设计，假定构建时的有效负载是受信任的，因而省略了运行时错误和边界检查。在RV32IMC架构上，它仅需要548至784字节的Flash和104至112字节的总RAM，与压缩率相匹配的块索引heatshrink和tamp相比，其小切片随机读取速度提升了数个数量级。
AI.summary: 本文针对资源受限微控制器提出了一种名为blaris的无窗口LZSS解压器。该方法通过将数据划分为带检查点的双向遍历流，直接在压缩有效负载中解析引用，消除了对RAM滑动窗口的依赖。在RV32IMC平台上，该算法以极低的Flash（548-784 B）和RAM（104-112 B）占用，实现了与高窗口传统解压器相近的压缩率，并大幅提升了小切片随机读取的性能。
AI.keywords: 微控制器, LZSS解压, 随机访问, 就地执行 (XIP), 无滑动窗口
AI.comments: 该论文的创新之处在于打破了传统LZ77/LZSS系算法在解压端必须在RAM中保留滑动窗口的限制，通过带有检查点的双向数据流直接在Flash/压缩载荷中回溯解析引用，极为契合RAM资源仅有几KB的超受限MCU及XIP（就地执行）场景。其局限性在于去除了运行时的错误与边界检查并假定数据可信，因此只适用于“主机端离线压缩、设备端部署”的受信场景，无法直接用于处理不受信的外部输入数据。

title: Done, But Still Working: Anytime Evaluation of When Coding Agents Should Stop
summary: Coding agents often continue working after their own tests pass. Does this additional work improve the patch, and how much could be saved by stopping earlier? We study these questions through anytime evaluation: replaying recorded runs, scoring intermediate patches with hidden tests, and measuring the cost incurred at each step. For policies that only stop a run or select an earlier patch, this allows paired comparisons without generating new trajectories, provided replay preserves the relevant states. Across about 6,000 runs of eight open models in two scaffolds on SWE-bench Verified, we find substantial differences in the value of continued work. The hindsight saving available at passing self-tests ranges from under 1% to 57%, depending on the model and scaffold. A rule that stops after the same patch passes twice saves 23% in a preregistered replication, but the preregistered quality test does not establish non-inferiority. We explain these differences by measuring how often a rule fires, how often the patch changes afterwards, and whether those changes repair or break it. Fine-tuning agents to imitate the rule saves 30% over six seeds, while quality preservation remains uncertain. Our results help identify both the opportunities and the risks of early stopping.

title: BRepA: Graph-Based B-Rep Pretraining for Unified CAD Understanding and Generation
summary: Boundary representation (B-Rep) of CAD models encodes geometric primitives and their relations as a graph structure, enabling efficient shape modeling within CAD software.
